stepsEvidence.heading: What To Look For
stepsEvidence.summary: ## What To Look For - New code that bypasses existing helpers, patterns, or abstractions without a clear reason - Duplicate logic that will drift - Overly broad abstractions for one call site - Tight coupling between modules that are otherwise separate - Business logic hidden in UI, handlers, config, or migration scripts - Hard-coded values that should be named, configured, or derived - Error messages or names that obscure the real behavior - Large functions where a small extraction would clarif

stepsEvidence.heading: How To Comment
stepsEvidence.summary: ## How To Comment Point to the repo pattern or maintenance cost. Good: Could we reuse `parseDateRange` here instead of adding a second parser? Keeping one path should make the timezone edge cases easier to maintain. Good: I might be missing the reason for the new dependency, but this looks like it only replaces a small amount of existing helper logic. Could we avoid adding it unless we need more of the library? Good: Could we keep the mapping close to the API adapter instead of the component? Th

stepsEvidence.heading: Severity
stepsEvidence.summary: ## Severity - `concern` for maintainability issues that will likely cause bugs or churn - `suggestion` for simpler structure or stronger alignment with local patterns - `question` when the author may have had a good trade-off in mind

reference.summary: description: Review React 19 test quality including coverage, patterns, and React 19 API testing. Use when reviewing tests or test coverage.

stepsEvidence.heading: Checklist
stepsEvidence.summary: - [ ] Components have tests for user interactions - [ ] Forms test both success and error paths - [ ] Server Actions tested in isolation - [ ] Custom hooks tested with `renderHook` - [ ] Edge cases covered (empty states, errors, loading) ### React 19 APIs - [ ] Forms using `useActionState` have tests - [ ] `useOptimistic` updates tested for immediate feedback - [ ] `useFormStatus` tested within form component context - [ ] Server Actions tested with mocked auth/database - [ ] `use()` hook tested

stepsEvidence.heading: Test Coverage
stepsEvidence.summary: - [ ] Components have tests for user interactions - [ ] Forms test both success and error paths - [ ] Server Actions tested in isolation - [ ] Custom hooks tested with `renderHook` - [ ] Edge cases covered (empty states, errors, loading)

stepsEvidence.heading: React 19 APIs
stepsEvidence.summary: - [ ] Forms using `useActionState` have tests - [ ] `useOptimistic` updates tested for immediate feedback - [ ] `useFormStatus` tested within form component context - [ ] Server Actions tested with mocked auth/database - [ ] `use()` hook tested with Promises and Context

stepsEvidence.heading: Testing Patterns
stepsEvidence.summary: - [ ] Using `@testing-library/react` and `@testing-library/user-event` - [ ] Queries prefer accessibility (`getByRole`, `getByLabelText`) - [ ] `waitFor` used for async assertions - [ ] Mocking external dependencies (API, database) - [ ] Tests are isolated and don't depend on each other

stepsEvidence.heading: Anti-Patterns
stepsEvidence.summary: - [ ] ❌ Testing implementation details (internal state, methods) - [ ] ❌ Querying by class names or data-testid when role available - [ ] ❌ Not waiting for async updates (`waitFor`) - [ ] ❌ Testing components without user interactions - [ ] ❌ Missing error case tests

stepsEvidence.heading: Server Action Testing
stepsEvidence.summary: - [ ] Server Actions tested as functions (not through UI) - [ ] Input validation tested - [ ] Authentication/authorization tested - [ ] Database operations mocked - [ ] Error handling tested

records.summary: The skill is a purely instructional review checklist for React 19 testing standards. It does not include executable code or access sensitive system resources, and its authorized tools are limited to passive reading and searching of files.
